content:
Dylan Brooks: looping in @Leila Farouk on E2E. We need a real test plan for safe-apply + rollback end-to-end before we start the staged rollout. Biggest worry is flakiness around async propagation + metric gates. What do you need from platform/staging?

Leila Farouk: thx. I can start wiring Playwright + API harness, but we need a stable staging target.
Main flows I want covered:
1) create config version (v1)
2) preflight validate (expect pass + diff payload)
3) apply canary (small blast radius) + wait for gates
4) force a failure scenario (validator warning or gate failure) and assert apply is blocked
5) rollback to v0 (one-click) and verify runtime state + audit events

Leila Farouk: questions:
- do we have a dedicated staging tenant + route that won’t be touched by humans?
- can we get deterministic metric gate signals? if p95/error rate depends on real traffic, tests will be noisy.

Chloe Martin: we can spin a dedicated tenant in staging, but we need to coordinate with release eng so it isn’t wiped on every seed. (we had this issue w/ console smoke tests)
For deterministic gates: we have a “gates override” flag internally but it’s not meant for prod. We could allow it in staging-only.

Jada Williams: gate evaluation reads from telemetry backend; in staging it can lag. That’s going to be your flake source.
We can add a “test mode” where gate window = 1m and uses a synthetic metric stream keyed by request_id, but that’s not built yet.

Felix Schneider: from Console side, compare view + history page calls list/get endpoints. For E2E we can mostly hit APIs and just do 1 UI smoke for rollback button.
But the UI does poll rollout status. If status is eventually consistent, Playwright will time out unless we bump waits.

Hannah Rivera: rollback flow is async job. Console shows progress + deep link to audit entry.
We should assert:
- job state transitions (queued -> applying -> completed)
- rollback emits audit events even on failure
- idempotency key returns same job id (repeat click scenario)

Aisha Bello: staging dashboards are not always reliable signals. For E2E can we gate on control-plane “propagation complete” + runtime ack instead of p95 latency? Like: runtime reports config version hash applied.

Jada Williams: +1. Gate on runtime ack is the only deterministic thing right now.
We can still test metric gate path with a stubbed metrics provider (staging-only) if we can get it prioritized.

Connor O'Brien: release perspective: we need a green E2E run that’s not flaky to make the phase-2 cutoff. If it flakes, it’ll get ignored.
If we can’t make metric gates deterministic, I’d rather split the tests:
- required: preflight + apply/rollback + audit + runtime ack
- optional/nightly: metric gates w/ best-effort

Tomáš Novák: +1 on splitting. Also: rollback under partial propagation is a big one.
Can we simulate a bad actor runtime shard that doesn’t ack? (like block one staging node)

Chloe Martin: we can add a “propagation simulator” in validator service, but that’s not runtime.
For runtime ack failures, Mateo’s team has a chaos switch in staging runtime that can drop apply messages for a scope. Not sure if it’s safe to use in CI.

Devon Price: FYI incident-bot will also post rollback links; if you want E2E to assert Slack notifications, we can expose a webhook sink in staging to capture payloads instead of actually posting.

Leila Farouk: ok, proposal:
E2E suite (CI, required):
A) baseline: seed v0, create v1 w/ small diff, preflight validate returns pass + diff contains changed fields
B) apply v1 (no metric gates) -> poll status until runtime ack -> assert audit: apply_attempted + applied
C) rollback to v0 -> poll until ack -> assert audit: rollback_attempted + rolled_back
D) idempotency: re-send rollback w/ same idempotency key -> returns same job id + no duplicate audit events

Leila Farouk: Nightly suite (allowed flaky-ish but should trend):
E) canary apply w/ metric gates enabled; use synthetic load generator to create stable latency/error; assert gate pass/fail behavior
F) partial propagation failure (if we can safely chaos one shard) -> ensure rollback still converges + status shows “degraded” and runbook link

Dylan Brooks: this is good. What staging requirements do you need written down?

Leila Farouk: minimum:
- dedicated staging tenant: `qa-e2e-optimize` with fixed customer_id (so we can filter versions cleanly)
- dedicated route/model combo that won’t be used by other tests
- feature flags ON in staging: config history store, rollback endpoint, runtime ack reporting
- ability to reset state between runs: delete versions for scope OR unique scope per run (e.g. suffix route with build id)

Hannah Rivera: unique scope per run is safer; delete endpoints are a whole can of worms and we probably don’t want that even in staging.
We can include a `test_scope_id` in metadata and just create a new route name each run.

Chloe Martin: we can support filtering by metadata in list endpoint? not sure it’s in scope.
But you can encode build id in route name and then list by scope.

Felix Schneider: if route name changes each run, Console UI smoke test needs to navigate to that scope. That’s fine if E2E uses direct deep link.

Aisha Bello: for polling: please don’t poll every 1s for 10 min, it will hammer staging. Use exponential backoff + max timeout.
Also we should add a single “rollout status” endpoint designed for polling.

Jada Williams: we already have a status endpoint; it’s not super optimized but ok.
One more flake: telemetry lag can make apply look “stuck” even though runtime applied.
If you use runtime ack as the source of truth for completion, you avoid that.

Connor O'Brien: action items?

Dylan Brooks: action items:
- @Chloe Martin to confirm staging tenant + route naming convention + flags by EOW
- @Jada Williams to confirm we can complete apply/rollback based on runtime ack (not metrics) and document expected states
- @Leila Farouk to draft the E2E test cases + required fixtures in Linear and call out what endpoints are needed
- @Devon Price optional: webhook sink for slack notification payloads (nice-to-have)

Leila Farouk: works. I’ll open an ENG subtask under the E2E ticket with the suite split + staging requirements.
Also: please make sure staging has stable runtime capacity; we’ve had GPU starvation causing timeouts in prior E2E.

Dylan Brooks: noted. I’ll ping SRE to keep staging capacity pinned during the beta window. :thumbsup:

Hannah Rivera: one more: rollback confirmation needs “justification” text for some roles. For E2E, we should use a service account w/ rollback perm that bypasses UI justification prompts (API still accepts reason).

Chloe Martin: API requires `reason` field anyway (for audit). Put `reason="e2e"`.

Leila Farouk: yep. will do.

Felix Schneider: (reaction) :eyes: on the deep link format. send me the URL shape you plan to use so Console routes it correctly.

Leila Farouk: will DM once I have it.

Devon Price: (reaction) :white_check_mark: re webhook sink, I can stub something quick in staging next week.
